summary: Core parsing, optimization, and the static build are in good shape, but I would not release this yet because the required browser/mobile acceptance path is still unverified in a real rendering environment.
strengths: `npm test` and `npm run build` both pass, and the output remains a frontend-only static bundle under `dist/`.
The parser in `src/lib/parseClipboard.js` covers the high-value validation rules: exact 10-player count, duplicate names, missing cells, supported tier aliases, and Korean error messages.

The optimizer in `src/lib/optimizer.js` looks technically sound: my independent sample-fixture and random-fixture cross-checks matched its score-difference, unranked-difference, and deterministic tie-break outputs.

findings.title: Release criteria for real browser/mobile behavior are still unverified
findings.detail: The only UI automation is the fake-DOM smoke test in `test/appFlow.test.js:11-79`, backed by the minimal harness in `testing/fakeDom.js:1-123`. That confirms `src/main.js` event wiring, but it does not execute CSS, viewport layout, or a real browser engine. `FINAL_OUTPUT.md:19-26` and `FINAL_OUTPUT.md:34-36` explicitly acknowledge that no served `dist/` browser smoke test was completed. Because the acceptance criteria require the workflow to be usable at `360px` width without horizontal overflow and GitHub Pages-ready as a static frontend, this is still missing release evidence.
findings.fix: Run and document a real browser-based smoke test against the built `dist/` app at both desktop and `360px` mobile width, or add headless browser automation that loads the built app, verifies the paste-to-result flow, and checks that the responsive layout does not overflow.

required_fixes: Add real browser or headless-browser verification for the built `dist/` app, including a `360px` mobile-width check and a standard desktop check.
Update handoff verification evidence after that run so release readiness is backed by actual browser results, not only fake-DOM coverage.
verification_run: `python3 -m http.server 4173 -d dist` (failed in this sandbox with `PermissionError: [Errno 1] Operation not permitted`)

`node --input-type=module` check on `src/fixtures/samplePlayers.tsv` confirmed 2 teams of 5, role counts `1/2/2`, 10 unique players, `scoreDifference=0`, `unrankedDifference=0`, `candidateCount=113400`
`node --input-type=module` independent optimizer cross-check matched library results on the sample fixture and on 5 random fixtures (`mismatches=0`)
release_readiness: Not release-ready. The core implementation is credible, but the required real-browser/mobile acceptance evidence is still absent.
